subject.title: Isolated cron consistently fails with "LLM request failed" on model-call-started phase

question: Should isolated cron recover after repeated run failures by resetting or retiring the run session, by landing only the bounded watchdog/fallback fixes, or by adding a different operator-visible recovery path?
rationale: The remaining reports span timeout hierarchy, provider fallback, and session recovery, and the suggested reset-after-N-errors policy changes user-visible cron behavior rather than being a purely mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Define Recovery Contract First
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers decide the isolated-cron reset, watchdog, and fallback semantics before queueing another automated fix.

options.title: Land Narrow Fixes Only
options.body: Proceed with the open watchdog/setup and stream-fallback fixes and leave cascading session reset for a later issue if failures persist.

options.title: Add Automatic Session Reset
options.body: Adopt the user-suggested reset-after-consecutive-errors policy and require focused proof that it does not hide provider, tool, or session-state failures.

recommendation.title: Define Recovery Contract First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers decide the isolated-cron reset, watchdog, and fallback semantics before queueing another automated fix.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest recent release and isolated cron/runtime routing signal among the identified owners, while the final behavior still needs maintainer review.
